Dear [redacted],

RE: TRACHEAL ADENOCARCINOMA - TREATMENT REVIEW

CLINICAL SUMMARY
You were diagnosed with tracheal adenocarcinoma T2N0, stage unknown, [redacted] 2023. Initial presentation with persistent cough and stridor. You underwent surgical resection [redacted] 2023 followed by adjuvant radiotherapy 54Gy/27# completed [redacted] 2023. Post-RT, commenced platinum-based chemo (cisplatin/pemetrexed) [redacted] 2024 for 4 cycles. CT [redacted] 2024 showed partial response with reduction in local disease.

MOLECULAR PROFILE
Genomic testing performed [redacted] 2024. No actionable mutations identified. TMB low (2.8 mut/Mb). MSI stable.

CURRENT STATUS
Recent CT chest [redacted] shows rapid progression with new pulmonary metastases bilateral, largest 2.3cm RLL. Local tracheal disease also increased significantly from prior. You report worsening dyspnoea, difficulty managing stairs, weight loss 8kg over 2 months. O/E: cachexia noted, reduced air entry both bases, no palpable lymphadenopathy.

COMORBIDITIES & SOCIAL HX
COPD - on inhalers, ex-smoker 30 pack-yrs quit [redacted] 2022. Type 2 DM diet-controlled. Lives alone, daughter visits weekly. Expressing significant anxiety re prognosis and functional decline.

PERFORMANCE STATUS
ECOG 3 - limited self-care, confined to bed/chair >50% waking hrs.

TREATMENT TOXICITY
Grade 2 radiation oesophagitis [redacted] 2023 - resolved. Grade 3 neutropenia during cycle 3 chemo [redacted] 2024 requiring dose reduction. Persistent grade 2 fatigue ongoing.

PLAN
Disease progression confirmed, limited further options given rare tumour type and poor PS. Discussed ceasing active oncological treatment. Referral to palliative care for symptom management and support. Follow-up [redacted] weeks or sooner if concerns.

Yours sincerely,
[redacted]
Consultant Medical Oncologist
